description: Analyze cargo unit graphs to detect unstable native build scripts

accepted.by: gary (in conversation, 2026-11-23: "accept the specs"; recorded by the implementing agent)

specs.given: A cargo project with native build scripts
specs.then: The tool reads unit graphs and compares them without invoking the compiler

specs.description: Command fails when no graphs are produced
specs.given: A cargo project with no unit graphs
specs.then: The tool exits with code 2 and reports the error

specs.given: A cargo project with default selections
specs.then: Only the specified selection is analyzed

specs.given: A cargo project
specs.then: The tool exits with code 2 and reports the invalid selection

specs.description: Unit graph is fetched with retries
specs.given: A cargo project with offline mode failing
specs.then: The tool retries without `--offline` and succeeds

specs.given: A cargo project where `cargo --unit-graph` fails
specs.then: The tool exits with code 2 and names the failing selection

specs.given: A cargo project with a build script depending on `cc`
specs.then: The script is identified as native and included in analysis

specs.given: A cargo project with a build script depending on `log`
specs.then: The script is not analyzed as native

specs.given: Any two identical unit graphs
specs.when: The tool computes keys for both
specs.then: The keys are identical

specs.description: Key includes features and profile settings
specs.given: A unit graph with a script's dependency tree
specs.then: The key includes package id, target name, mode, sorted features, and profile settings except name

specs.given: A native script with two distinct keys
specs.then: The script is marked unstable with groups and differences

specs.given: A native script with one key
specs.then: The script is marked stable

specs.description: Every unstable finding carries a hint for each kind it shows, marked as a prediction
specs.given: Any unstable native script whose differing units have any mix of kinds
specs.then: For each of `profile` and `features` present among its units the report carries that kind's hint, and every hint says it is a prediction from the unit graph

specs.given: A project with no unstable scripts
specs.then: The tool exits with code 0

specs.given: A project with at least one unstable script
specs.then: The tool exits with code 1

specs.given: A project with `.hexa/project.json` containing `build_keys.enabled: true`
specs.then: The build-keys check is executed and one line is printed

specs.given: A project with `.hexa/project.json` containing `build_keys.enabled: false`
specs.then: The build-keys check is not executed

specs.description: A hint matches its kind and never claims more than a prediction
specs.given: A unit-graph comparison whose only difference is the profile
specs.then:
The hint names the `[profile.

.build-override]` change, does not suggest a workspace-hack crate, and says it is a prediction from the unit graph rather than a measured result

specs.description: The profile name is not part of the key
specs.given: Two selections whose trees for one native script are identical except that the profile is named `dev` in one and `test` in the other, with the same settings
specs.then: The two keys are equal and the script is not unstable

specs.description: Unstable is exactly two or more keys
specs.given: Any native script and any set of selections containing it
specs.then: It is `unstable` exactly when its keys take two or more distinct values; the groups partition those selections by key; at most ten differing units are listed, each with kind features, profile or presence

specs.description: A features difference gets the workspace-hack hint
specs.given: A native script whose trees differ only in a dependency's feature set between `build` and `test --no-run`
specs.then: The hint says to pin the unified feature set as a build-dependency of a crate every selection includes, as a cargo-hakari `workspace-hack` crate does, and that it is a prediction from the unit graph
